tasks.personal-social-wellbeing-t2: Topic: Personal and Social Well-being. Cover friendships, relationship problems, conflict resolution, personal safety, responsibilities, trusted adults, safe choices, and study habits. Ask learners to identify healthy friendship behaviours, choose fair ways to solve a conflict, recognise responsible study habits, or decide when to ask a trusted adult for help.
tasks.physical-education-t2: Topic: Physical Education. Cover invasion games, catching and passing, agility, teamwork, fair play, repeated drills, and simple tactics in small-sided games. Ask learners to identify good passing or defending choices, explain agility and teamwork, recognise fair-play behaviour, or choose the best tactic in a mini-game situation.
tasks.creative-arts-t2: Topic: Creative Arts. Cover texture, pattern, printmaking, collage, storytelling, puppetry, rhythm patterns, voice, movement, rehearsal, and presentation. Ask learners to identify visual art techniques, recognise repeated patterns or rhythms, choose effective storytelling or puppetry decisions, or answer simple performance and artwork process questions.
tasks.bullying-getting-help-t2: Topic: Bullying for Grade 6 Life Skills (CAPS term 2 Personal and Social Well-being). Cover what bullying is (hurting again and again, on purpose), the kinds (physical, words, leaving out and rumours, online), reasons why some children bully, that it is never the fault of the child who is bullied, where to find help (a trusted adult, a teacher, a school counsellor, Childline on 116, which is free), not hitting back, how a child who bullies can stop, and what a bystander can do. Write for 11 to 12 year olds in plain words with no graphic detail. Ask scenario and recall questions.
tasks.cultural-rites-of-passage-t2: Topic: Cultural rites of passage for Grade 6 Life Skills (CAPS term 2). Cover that a rite of passage marks an important stage of life, the stages of birth, baptism, a wedding and death, the meaning, the personal significance and the social significance of each stage, that cultures and religions in South Africa mark them in different ways and that each deserves respect, and being kind to a classmate who is grieving. Treat all cultures and religions respectfully and equally, and do not describe any ritual in detail. Write for 11 to 12 year olds.
